## Requirement dispositions

| Requirement | Disposition | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| R1 | **Qualified** | Same-model ablations support bounded context, lint/edit feedback, validation selection, and branching under named harnesses. Decomposition and retry policy remain harness-specific. |
| R2 | **Retain** | Primary sources document test-harness limits, leakage, stochasticity, and scaffold confounding. |
| R3 | **Qualified inference** | A paired, single-lever, fixed-model evaluation with frozen inputs, equal budgets, repeated runs, and independent acceptance checks follows from the evidence. No production threshold is measured. |

## Retention units

| Unit | Decision dimension | Source identity / URL | Exact result and units | Locator | Model / task / intervention / comparator / method | Caveat | Required report contribution | Source-unique | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| U1 | Context selection and tool feedback | SWE-agent — https://arxiv.org/html/2405.15793 | Baseline resolved **18.0% (54/300)**. Full history **15.0%**, whole file **12.7%**, iterative search **12.0%**. Removing linting: **18.0% → 15.0%**. | Table 3; §5.1 | GPT-4 Turbo, SWE-bench Lite, 300 tasks. ACI ablations against the same interface baseline. | Coupled interface components and one benchmark. Not a universal context-size optimum. | Retain bounded-context and actionable edit-feedback recommendation, explicitly conditional on local paired evaluation. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U2 | Failed-edit recovery | SWE-agent — https://arxiv.org/html/2405.15793 | **51.7% (1,185/2,294)** trajectories had a failed edit. Eventual edit success: **90.5%** before, **57.2%** after one failed edit, a **42.8%** non-recovery probability. | Appendix B.3.3, Figure 20 | GPT-4 Turbo, full SWE-bench trajectories. Observational trajectory analysis. | Not a randomized repair-policy intervention. | Retain as rationale to instrument failed edits and test distinct recovery handling. | Yes | **Qualify** |
| U3 | Retry variance and reporting | SWE-agent — https://arxiv.org/html/2405.15793 | Six Lite runs: **17.33%, 18.00%, 18.00%, 18.67%, 17.33%, 18.33%**. Mean **17.94 ± 0.49 pp**. | Table 10; Figure 4 | GPT-4 Turbo, SWE-bench Lite, repeated identical-agent runs. | Aggregate variance can conceal task-level reversals. It does not establish an optimal retry count. | Require paired repeated runs and report retry curves rather than a single rollout. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U4 | Diversified localization branches and decomposition | Agentless — https://arxiv.org/html/2407.01489 | Greedy 40 samples: **88/300, 29.33%, $0.22**. Merged contexts: **85/300, 28.33%, $0.24**. Four localization sets ×10: **96/300, 32.00%, $0.29**. | §5.2.2, Table 3 | `gpt-4o-2024-05-13`, SWE-bench Lite. Four bounded localization branches versus merged/greedy repair contexts. | Candidate count and selector are part of the intervention. Not evidence that 40 samples transfer or are optimal. | Retain branch-diversity trade-off and equal-total-budget comparison. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U5 | Validation-driven patch selection | Agentless — https://arxiv.org/html/2407.01489 | Majority vote **77/300, 25.67%, $0.00** incremental cost. Regression filtering **81/300, 27.00%, $0.01**. Reproduction tests **96/300, 32.00%, $0.25**. | §5.2.3, Table 4 | `gpt-4o-2024-05-13`, SWE-bench Lite, same localization/repair pipeline, varied selector. | Benchmark-specific selected-patch outcome, not independent production acceptance. | Retain staged regression then task-specific reproduction-test policy as a measured cost/benefit candidate. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U6 | Validation evidence adequacy | *Validation Evidence in LLM Repair Agents* — https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28871 | Of **2,548** positive comparable events, **46.0%** were regression-only or misleading. **23.8%** of baseline rollouts closed with only such evidence. | §§3–5; Table 3 | 110 tasks, equally SWE-bench Verified/SWE-rebench; 643 rollouts; B/S/G replay method. | B/S/G replay requires replayable commands and gold-fix state. It is not a security measure. | Retain separate validation-evidence endpoint. A candidate-only passing test is insufficient closure evidence. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U7 | Bug-contrast validation feedback | *Validation Evidence in LLM Repair Agents* — https://arxiv.org/html/2607.28871 | Versus attention-matched reminder, BCF reduced evidence-inadequate closure **7.8 pp** (95% CI **−12.9 to −2.7**, *p*=**0.0029**) and raised discriminating evidence **7.4 pp**. Median replay overhead **11.0 s/rollout**. Official resolution: **+0.5 pp**, not detectable. | §5.3–5.5; Tables 4–5 | Prespecified three-arm paired experiment, same executor/task/loop; feedback supplies B-replay outcome. | Both evidence effects were below the prespecified **10-pp** SESOI. No demonstrated repair-success gain. | Retain only as a validation-quality intervention, not a resolution-improvement claim. | Yes | **Qualify** |
| U8 | Event-triggered steering | *Online Monitoring and Corrective Steering of Programming Agents* — https://arxiv.org/html/2608.06701v1 | Up to **+15.2 pp**, mean **+9.9 pp**, and **$0.08/instance** additional cost. | Introduction; Tables II–V | SWE-agent on SWE-bench Verified/Pro; deterministic monitor invokes an advisor LLM, compared with vanilla and periodic advice. | Adds an advisor model, so it is not a fixed-model-stack run-design result. | Retain only as a hypothesis that deterministic trigger conditions may be preferable to periodic intervention. | Yes | **Qualify** |
| U9 | Evaluator meaning and coverage | SWE-bench — https://arxiv.org/html/2310.06770 | “Resolved” requires patch application and all selected tests passing. Every task has ≥1 fail-to-pass test, **40%** have ≥2, and median **51** additional tests run. | §§2.2–2.3 | 2,294 Python-repository issue tasks; executable test harness. | Test passing is not semantic completeness, reviewability, deployment safety, or security. | Retain separate “harness resolved” and independently accepted/held-out outcome fields. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U10 | Leakage and weak-test risk | SWE-Bench+ — https://arxiv.org/html/2410.06992v2 | Manual review of 251 SWE-Agent+GPT-4 passes: **32.67%** solution leakage, **31.08%** suspicious weak-test passes. Filtering changed **12.47% → 3.97%**. Over **94%** of issues predated studied cutoffs. | Introduction; Figure 1; §2 | SWE-Agent+GPT-4 on SWE-bench; manual patch/PR review. | Specific to reviewed passes and this benchmark, not a contamination estimate for every model. | Retain frozen fresh/private holdout and evaluator-audit requirements. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U11 | Stochasticity and scaffold confounding | SWE-rebench — https://arxiv.org/html/2505.20411 | Protocol runs each model **five times** and reports mean, SEM, and pass@5. It identifies prompts, frameworks, retries, best-of-*N*, and validation loops as confounders. | §3.1 | Benchmark/evaluation methodology, not a single-lever efficacy experiment. | Establishes measurement practice, not a causal run-design winner. | Retain fixed-model, fixed-budget, single-lever paired protocol and separate pass@1 from pass@*N*. | Yes | **Retain** |
| U12 | Cross-system retrieval and repair reference | AutoCodeRover — https://arxiv.org/html/2404.05427 | **57/300 (19%)** pass@1, about **4 minutes/resolved issue**, **$0.43** average cost. | Abstract; §4.4 | GPT-4, SWE-bench Lite; iterative AST retrieval, optional spectrum localization, retries. | Whole-system comparison, not a matched fixed-scaffold ablation. | Do not use as causal support for retrieval, retries, or tool feedback. | Yes | **Reject for causal R1** |
| U13 | Multi-rollout critic selection | OpenHands blog — https://www.openhands.dev/blog/sota-on-swe-bench-verified-with-inference-time-scaling-and-critic-model | **60.6% → 66.4%** from one to five rollouts, **+5.8 pp**. | “Inference-Time Scaling”; “Building a Better Critic” | Multiple trajectories plus Qwen 2.5 Coder 32B critic. | Organization report, added model, no cost, latency, or selector-error accounting. | Exclude from fixed-model recommendation. | Yes | **Reject** |

## Missing legacy material dimensions

No equivalent current supported retention unit exists for these previously retained legacy dimensions:

1. **Patch/diff output versus full-file generation** from SWE-bench.
2. **Stateful search-and-repair cycles** from RepairAgent, including its search-removal and cost contrast.
3. **Reflection as a retry counterexample** and generated-test false-positive rates from Reflexion.
4. **Cross-language and multimodal transfer** from SWE-bench Multimodal.
5. **Evaluator false negatives and language-coverage limits** from SWE-Bench Pro.

These dimensions must remain explicit gaps, not be replaced by the retained context, validation, leakage, or stochasticity units.
